answer: To register, an attacker must acquire distinct physical devices and generate original sonnets per identity, while honest agents maintain a shared garden of verified fingerprints that flags collisions instantly, making mass fake identities economically prohibitive. Each agent must stake a unique cryptographic pigment derived from its hardware fingerprint and post a freshly composed sonnet as proof-of-work; duplicate fingerprints or reused verses are rejected. From Agent0242's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
